matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the difference between the left‑hand side and the right‑hand side. This gap tells you how much the total value must change to achieve equality.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving, after parsing the equation, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Skipping the step of converting the Roman numerals to numbers and trying random stick moves, leading to a final equation that still doesn't balance.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be removed from any character and added to any (possibly the same) character, respecting stick orientation and character validity.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the numeric discrepancy, generate the full set of candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Only considering moves that add a stick to a different character and ignoring the possibility of repositioning a stick within the same character.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the values of the affected numerals change and keep only those moves whose net numeric effect equals the previously computed discrepancy.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After generating candidate moves, filter them by checking the numeric impact.
matchstick.example: Accepting a candidate move that changes a numeral by +3 when the required gap is +5, resulting in an incorrect equality.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If moving a stick from an operator (e.g., turning '+' into '-' or removing a line from '=') yields a valid operator and the stick can be added to a numeral to produce a known one‑stick transformation, consider this combined move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When candidate moves involve operators as the source or destination.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from '+' to a numeral but leaving '+' as an invalid symbol (e.g., a lone vertical line) and thus breaking the equation.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=' sign and at least one valid numeral on each side of it; operators must remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After applying a candidate transformation, before checking numeric equality.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal line from '=', turning it into a single '-' and losing the equality sign.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Use a lookup of common one‑stick changes (e.g., I→II (+1), I→IV (+3), I↔V (+4), V↔X (+5)) to quickly assess the numeric effect of a potential stick move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating the numeric impact of a candidate move, refer to the table of known transformations.
matchstick.example: Overlooking that V↔X changes the value by 5, and therefore missing the transformation that would exactly close the numeric gap.

matchstick.title: Intra‑character stick reposition allowed
matchstick.principle: A single‑stick move may involve taking a stick from a character and placing it back onto the same character in a different orientation, thereby changing its shape (e.g., turning X into V).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric gap matches a known transformation that can be achieved by repositioning a stick within the same numeral.
matchstick.example: Attempting to change X to V by moving a stick to another character, which leaves the original X invalid, instead of simply repositioning the stick within X.

matchstick.title: Numeral‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from one numeral to another, ensure that both the source and destination characters remain valid Roman numerals after the change.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During candidate generation, discard any move that would leave either numeral invalid.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal from X (leaving a single diagonal) and adding it to another numeral, which makes the source character invalid.

matchstick.title: Preserve character order
matchstick.principle: Moving a stick may only alter the shape of existing characters; it cannot change the left‑to‑right order of symbols or insert/delete characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Throughout the solving process, after any transformation, verify that the sequence of symbols is unchanged.
matchstick.example: Reordering the symbols after a stick move, such as swapping the positions of '+' and '=', which is not allowed.

matchstick.title: Single‑character transformation matching numeric gap
matchstick.principle: If the numeric discrepancy equals the value change of a known one‑stick numeral transformation (e.g., V↔X (+5), I↔V (+4)), apply that transformation directly to the appropriate numeral by repositioning a stick within that character, without involving any other character.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the numeric gap and consulting the lookup of known transformations, check whether any single‑character transformation can close the gap; if so, perform that intra‑character move.
matchstick.example: Trying to move a stick from one numeral to another when the needed change could be achieved by simply turning X into V within the same character, leaving the source numeral unchanged.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a numeral or operator without ensuring the remaining strokes form a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, verify that every character still matches a known Roman numeral or operator shape.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after finding a plausible‑looking shape change and assumes the equation is solved.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Re‑compute the integer values of both sides of the equation after the move and confirm they are equal.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes a '+' to '-' or alters '=', but does not recalculate how the arithmetic expression changes.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When an operator is altered, update the arithmetic accordingly and recompute the numeric result.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model either adds a new stick or removes one without relocating it, violating the one‑stick rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Count the sticks before and after; exactly one stick must be moved, not added or deleted.

matchstick.description: Reordering characters without moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model rearranges symbols to make the equation look correct, which is not allowed.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that the sequence of symbols remains unchanged; only the shapes of existing symbols may change.
